chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it (marfu'), said:
Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) said: 'When the sheep is slaughtered and skinned, or something from it is stripped before it dies, eating it is not permissible.'

key_terms.ذُبِحَتِ: ritually slaughtered (dhubihat) — the Islamic method of slaughter involving severing the throat
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: marfu' — a hadith term indicating the chain is elevated/raised to a higher authority without naming all intermediaries
key_terms.سُلِخَتْ: skinned/flayed — removing the hide from the slaughtered animal
key_terms.يَحِلَّ: become permissible (yahilla) — from the root h-l-l meaning halal/lawful

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat an animal that was skinned before it fully died after slaughter in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) establishes a key condition for the validity of ritual slaughter: the animal must be fully dead before any skinning or flaying begins. If the sheep is skinned — even partially — while still alive after slaughter, the meat becomes forbidden to eat. This ruling addresses a practical concern in traditional butchering where speed might lead to premature skinning, and reflects the Islamic principle that the animal's life must have properly ceased before processing begins.
